steps.observation: You have 300 seconds. Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
# The Last Light

Old Marcus had kept the light burning for thirty-one years.

Every evening at dusk, he climbed the 112 steps — he had counted them so many times the number lived in his bones — and he lit the lamp. Every morning at dawn, he climbed back up and extinguished it. In between, he listened to the sea.

Most people assumed the job was lonely. They said so whenever the supply boat came, tilting their heads with that particular brand of pity reserved for hermits and widowers. Marcus never corrected them. Loneliness required wanting something you didn't have, and Marcus had everything he needed.

He had the gulls. He had his coffee, black and burnt the way he preferred it. He had the logbook, where he recorded weather and passing vessels in his cramped, careful handwriting.

And he had the light itself.

On the night of the November storm — the bad one, the one that would make the mainland newspapers — Marcus climbed his steps while the wind screamed against the glass like something alive. The lamp flickered. His heart seized.

He cupped his hands around the flame as a father might cup a child's face.

It held.

Somewhere out in the darkness, a freighter altered its course by two degrees and slipped safely into harbor.

Marcus never knew their names. He never needed to.

He descended his 112 steps, made his burnt coffee, and listened to the sea say *thank you* in the only language it knew.
